# BUG-015: Auto-Generated CLAUDE.md via Manifest Detection

## Problem

When a developer runs `install.sh --project` or `install.ps1 -Project`, the installer copies `project-template/CLAUDE.md` verbatim into the target project. Every field in `## Development Commands` (`Build`, `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, `Setup`) is set to the literal placeholder `<command>`, and `## Project Identity` fields (`Name`, `Description`, `Stack`) are blank. The agent starts work blindly, wastes tokens guessing commands that already exist in `package.json` or `go.mod`, and the developer must manually fill in values that can be detected automatically.

## Solution

Introduce `scripts/detect-stack.mjs`, a read-only Node.js script that performs a `readdir` sweep of the project root and — when a monorepo indicator is found (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `melos.yaml`, or a `workspaces` array in root `package.json`) — expands workspace glob patterns using the multi-wildcard algorithm (see Alternative paths) to discover workspace subdirectories, then issues one `readdir` per resolved directory. Melos monorepos are handled by line-scanning `melos.yaml` for its `packages:` list rather than hardcoding directory names. Workspace directories are sorted lexicographically before the detector pass to ensure cross-OS determinism. The root sweep result and each subdirectory file list are distributed to detectors; no detector calls `readdir` independently. The script emits a JSON object on stdout containing all detectable fields. Both the installer (at `--project` install time) and `/cc-init` Step 2 (at session start) call this script, then surgically fill in only the blank/placeholder lines of CLAUDE.md. Fields the developer has already customized are never overwritten. Interactive questions are asked only for fields the script could not resolve — unless the environment is non-interactive (see CI/CD mode below). **Minimum Node.js version: 18.0.0** (`fs.promises.readdir` with `{ withFileTypes: true }` and top-level `await` in ESM require Node ≥ 18; the `engines` field in the installer's own `package.json` already enforces `node >= 20`, which satisfies this requirement).

## Behavior

### Main path

1. Developer runs `./install.sh --project` (or `install.ps1 -Project`) inside a project directory containing a `package.json`, `go.mod`, or similar manifest.
2. Installer resolves the absolute project root (`cd "$projDir" && pwd` / `Resolve-Path`).
3. Installer calls `node scripts/detect-stack.mjs <abs-root>` and captures stdout via `| Out-String` (PS) or command substitution (bash).
4. `detect-stack.mjs` runs one `fs.promises.readdir` sweep, distributes the file list to all detectors in priority order, merges results, trims all string values, and writes `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n'` to stdout. All errors go to stderr. Exit code is always 0.
5. Installer reads current CLAUDE.md content. For each target field, it checks whether the line currently contains the `<command>` placeholder or is blank after `: ` (CRLF-resilient regex). If yes → replaces with the detected value (no secondary unescaping — `ConvertFrom-Json` / `JSON.parse` values are already unescaped runtime strings). If no → skips.
6. CLAUDE.md is written once with all resolvable fields populated. Remaining `<command>` placeholders stay for `/cc-init` to handle.
7. Developer opens Claude Code and runs `/cc-init`.
8. `/cc-init` Step 2 re-runs `detect-stack.mjs` with the absolute project root and extracts fields from the JSON output using Node.js inline evaluation — **`jq` is not used** (prohibited by global constraint). **`jq` is not used** (prohibited by global constraint). Field values are extracted using a Node.js inline script that emits one JSON-encoded line per property to avoid corruption from multiline values (e.g. a `description` field containing a newline would break a naïve `key=value` split):

```bash
# bash
node scripts/detect-stack.mjs "$root" | node -e "
  const chunks=[];process.stdin.on('data',d=>chunks.push(d));
  process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
    const d=JSON.parse(chunks.join(''));
    Object.entries(d).forEach(([k,v])=>console.log(JSON.stringify([k,v])));
  });
"
```

```powershell
# PowerShell
$raw = node scripts/detect-stack.mjs $root | Out-String
$obj = try { $raw | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { $null }
if ($obj) {
  $obj.PSObject.Properties | ForEach-Object {
    $val = $_.Value
    # Serialize non-string types to compact JSON before encoding
    $str = if ($val -is [string]) { $val }
            elseif ($val -eq $null) { '' }
            else { $val | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 5 }
    $b64 = [System.Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($str))
    "$($_.Name)=$b64"
  }
}
```

In bash, each emitted line is a two-element JSON array `["key","value"]`; the agent parses it with `node -e 'const [k,v]=JSON.parse(process.argv[1]); ...'`. This approach is safe regardless of what characters the value contains. In PowerShell, values are Base64-encoded to a single line before transmission and decoded after. Only fields still absent from the JSON trigger interactive questions (batched, not one-at-a-time).
9. CLAUDE.md is updated with a single surgical `Edit` call — no full-file rewrite.

### Alternative paths

- **Monorepo (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` / `pkg.workspaces` / `melos.yaml`):** detector adjusts build/setup commands to `pnpm -r build` / `melos bootstrap` etc. **Indicator precedence when multiple coexist:** `pnpm-workspace.yaml` > `melos.yaml` > `package.json workspaces` array. The highest-priority indicator determines the package-manager command set (`pnpm -r …` vs `melos …` vs `npm -w …`); all coexisting indicators still contribute their listed workspace glob patterns to the combined `workspaceDirs` expansion — patterns from lower-priority indicators are appended (after deduplication) so no workspace subdirectory is missed. If both `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `package.json workspaces` list the same directory, deduplication removes the duplicate before the detector pass. Workspace entries under `workspaces` may be glob patterns (e.g. `"apps/*"`, `"packages/**"`). Expansion algorithm (no external deps, handles multi-wildcard patterns): (a) Split the pattern into path segments by `/`. (b) Walk segments left to right until the first segment containing `*` or `?` is encountered — all segments before it form the `baseDir`. (c) Call `fs.promises.readdir(baseDir, { withFileTypes: true })` and filter to entries where `isDirectory()` is true and the entry name matches the wildcard segment using only single-segment matching (`*` matches any sequence of non-`/` chars, `?` matches exactly one non-`/` char; `**` in position zero of a segment is treated as `*` — deep traversal is out of scope). (d) The remaining pattern segments after the wildcard segment are joined and appended to each matched directory name; if any further `*`/`?` remain, those nested globs are resolved with one additional `readdir` call per level, capped at `CC_GLOB_DEPTH` levels of recursion (default 5; set via environment variable before calling detect-stack.mjs, e.g. `CC_GLOB_DEPTH=8 node scripts/detect-stack.mjs <root>`). The cap prevents runaway expansion on pathological patterns; enterprise layouts with deeper nesting can raise it without code changes. Each terminal resolved path is added to `workspaceDirs` and given one `readdir` call for manifest detection. Melos monorepos: parse `melos.yaml` for the `packages:` list (YAML scalar strings, no external YAML parser — extract lines under `packages:` via line-by-line scan until the next top-level key; for each extracted line apply the following normalization before treating it as a glob pattern: (1) trim leading/trailing whitespace; (2) strip a single leading `-` character followed by one or more spaces (YAML block sequence indicator); (3) strip a single leading `"` and trailing `"`, or leading `'` and trailing `'`, if both are present (YAML scalar quoting); (4) strip inline comments: after quote-stripping, remove everything from the first unquoted `#` character to end-of-line; (5) strip YAML anchors and aliases: remove `&\w+` (anchor definition) and `*\w+` (alias reference) tokens that appear at the start of or within the value — aliased paths are not resolved (alias expansion requires a full YAML parser), so if the normalized value after anchor/alias removal is empty, skip the line; (6) handle YAML flow sequences: if the `packages:` key is followed on the same line by `[` (e.g. `packages: [apps/*, packages/*]`), extract the content between `[` and `]`, split on `,`, and apply normalizations (1)–(5) to each element; (7) handle block scalars and folded blocks: if the `packages:` key is followed by `|` or `>` on the same line, the scanner treats all subsequent indented lines as raw text content until the indentation level returns to the `packages:` key level or a new top-level key is found. Each indented content line is then subject to normalizations (1)–(5). Block scalar chomping indicators (`|-`, `|+`, `>-`, `>+`) are recognized and stripped before text processing; (8) skip the line if empty or starts with `#` after all normalizations). Fall back to `apps/` and `packages/` only if `melos.yaml` is missing or its `packages:` block is absent. Only the first workspace `package.json` that contains a known framework dependency is used for framework identification — the root `package.json` takes priority if it also contains a framework dep.
- **Angular with version pin:** `@angular/core` major version extracted from the first `package.json` in the priority chain (root first, then workspace subdirs in sorted iteration order) that contains `@angular/core` in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. Version normalization before extracting major: (1) strip leading `^`, `~`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `=` characters; (2) if the value starts with `workspace:` (e.g. `workspace:*`, `workspace:^20.0.0`), strip the `workspace:` prefix and any following semver modifier, then extract the first digit sequence; (3) split on `.` and take index 0 as the major version string; (4) if the result is not a non-empty numeric string, skip and continue to the next candidate. Result appended to stack string (e.g. `"Angular 20"`). If no `@angular/core` is found at any level, the detector falls through to the next entry in the priority list.
- **Multiple manifests (polyglot repo):** when two or more language manifests coexist at the project root (e.g. `package.json` + `go.mod`), the conflict is resolved field-by-field using the detector priority order; the highest-priority detector that returns a non-null value for each field wins. The `stack` field concatenates all detected language names in detector priority order, joined with `/` (no spaces), lower-case (e.g. `"typescript/go"` for two languages, `"typescript/go/python"` for three). The `/`-delimiter and priority-order rule apply regardless of how many languages are detected; there is no cap on the number of concatenated names. All other fields (`build`, `test`, etc.) use the single highest-priority non-null value. **Same-depth workspace conflicts** (two workspace subdirs at the same directory level, each with a different framework): detectors are applied across all workspace manifest files simultaneously; for each field, the detector priority list determines the winner regardless of which subdirectory the manifest came from. If two subdirs match the same detector at the same priority (e.g. two React apps), the subdir that appears first in **sorted** order wins — `workspaceDirs` is deduplicated (same resolved absolute path → keep one entry) then sorted lexicographically (using `Array.prototype.sort()` with no locale argument, i.e. Unicode code-point order) before the detector pass. Deduplication occurs before sorting and before any detector runs. Since a real filesystem cannot have two directories with the same absolute path, deduplication only matters when multiple glob patterns resolve to the same directory (e.g. `apps/*` and `apps/web` both resolving `apps/web`). After deduplication and sorting there is always a unique first entry per group, so no further tie-breaker is needed.
- **Empty or invalid `workspaces` field in `package.json`:** if the `workspaces` property is present but is an empty array (`[]`), the monorepo indicator is still set (`"monorepo": true`) but no workspace glob patterns are expanded — `workspaceDirs` is omitted from the output. If `workspaces` is an object (Yarn workspaces v1 style: `{ "packages": [...] }`), the `packages` array inside is extracted and treated as the glob pattern list. If `workspaces` is a string, `null`, a number, or any other non-array non-object type, it is ignored entirely (field treated as absent). Multi-statement build/test commands (e.g. `npm run build && npm run lint`) are stored verbatim as a single string — they are not split on `&&`, `;`, `||`, or pipe characters. The value written to CLAUDE.md is the exact string from the manifest `scripts` field, trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace only. Package-manager commands (`pnpm -r …` etc.) are still set based on the lock-file indicator.
- **Exclusion patterns in `package.json workspaces` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:** entries beginning with `!` (e.g. `"!apps/internal"`) are exclusion rules. For `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the `packages:` block is line-scanned for YAML sequence entries starting with `!` after the same normalizations applied to `melos.yaml` (step 1–3 from the Melos YAML normalization); each `!`-prefixed entry is treated as a negative glob and applied to remove resolved paths from `workspaceDirs` using the same path-prefix matching. Exclusion entries are collected in a separate set and applied after all positive patterns are fully expanded and deduplicated. The glob expansion algorithm collects positive patterns first, then removes any resolved path that matches a negative pattern. Exclusion matching is path-prefix comparison against the resolved absolute path, not a re-glob; `!apps/internal` removes `<root>/apps/internal` from `workspaceDirs` if it was added by an earlier positive pattern. Negative patterns are never passed to `readdir`.
- **Hard ceiling for `CC_GLOB_DEPTH`:** the environment variable is parsed as a decimal integer; values above 20 are clamped to 20 (the hard ceiling). Values below 1 are clamped to 1. Non-numeric values fall back to the default of 5. This prevents pathological inputs from bypassing the cap.
- **Circular symlinks and path isolation:** before adding any resolved path to `workspaceDirs`, the script calls `fs.promises.realpath` and verifies: (a) the real path starts with the project root (`realpath.startsWith(rootRealpath + path.sep)` — uses `path.sep` not `/` for Windows compatibility); (b) the path was not already visited (tracked in a `Set<string>` of realpaths). **Symlinks pointing outside the project root are explicitly rejected** — if `realpath` resolves to a path that does not start with `rootRealpath + path.sep`, the entry is skipped with `WARN: symlink target outside project root — skipped: <path>`. This is an intentional security boundary; there is no option to disable it. If either check (a) or (b) fails the entry is skipped. The `realpath` call is made inside a try/catch; if it throws (dangling symlink), the entry is skipped with a WARN.
- **Glob pattern resolves to a file instead of a directory:** during glob expansion, after calling `fs.promises.readdir(baseDir, { withFileTypes: true })`, the filter step checks `isDirectory()` before adding an entry to `workspaceDirs`. Entries where `isDirectory()` returns `false` (including symlinks to files, regular files, device nodes) are silently skipped — no WARN is emitted, because it is normal for `*` patterns to match mixed file/dir entries in a workspace root. A WARN is only emitted if the pattern explicitly contained a known directory segment (e.g. `apps/web`) but `isDirectory()` returned false, indicating an unexpected file at a named location.
- **Absolute paths in workspace glob entries:** if a workspace glob entry resolves to an absolute path (starts with `/` on POSIX or a drive letter `C:\` on Windows), it is treated as a security violation and rejected with `WARN: absolute path in workspace entry rejected: <entry>`. Workspace entries must always be relative to the project root. The `realpath` boundary check (which rejects paths outside the project root) would also catch these, but the explicit check fires first for clarity.
- **Corrupted or unreadable `melos.yaml`:** the `melos.yaml` line-scan is wrapped in try/catch at the file-read level. If `readFile` throws, the file is treated as absent and the fallback dirs (`apps/`, `packages/`) are used. If `readFile` succeeds but the content yields zero valid package entries after normalization (e.g. the file has valid YAML syntax but an empty or structurally unexpected `packages:` block), the fallback dirs are also used. Melos YAML is never parsed with a full YAML parser; any YAML construct not handled by the line-scan normalizations (steps 1–8) causes that line to be skipped — it does not abort the scan.
- **Nested workspace definitions (monorepo-in-monorepo):** if a resolved workspace subdir itself contains a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `melos.yaml`, or `package.json` with a `workspaces` array, those nested workspace indicators are **not** recursively expanded. The inner workspace is treated as a single unit — its own root manifest is scanned by detectors, but its sub-packages are not added to the outer `workspaceDirs`. This prevents unbounded recursion in deeply nested enterprise layouts.
- **Go workspace (`go.work`) with parent-directory paths:** `go.work` `use` directives are parsed for lines matching `/^\s*use\s+(\S+)/` (not anchored to `./`). Paths starting with `../` are parent-directory references that resolve outside the project root — these are rejected with `WARN: go.work use directive points outside project root — skipped: <path>` (same `realpath` boundary check as other workspace entries). Paths starting with `./` or bare directory names are resolved relative to the go.work file's location. The `go.work` path (`replace` and `require` directives) are not parsed — only `use` directives contribute `workspaceDirs`. After `realpath` and deduplication, `use` paths are merged into `workspaceDirs` alongside any other workspace indicators; if a path was already added by another indicator, the deduplication step removes the duplicate. that are resolved to absolute paths and appended to `workspaceDirs` (subject to deduplication, sorting, and the `realpath` safety check). The `go` field in the output reflects all module paths detected; `stack` is still `"go"`. This supplements root `go.mod` detection for multi-module Go workspaces.
- **Conflicting cross-ecosystem manifests in a workspace subdir:** if a workspace subdir contains both `package.json` and `go.mod` (or any other combination of language manifests), the same polyglot detection rules applied at the root are applied there too — `stack` for that subdir is `/`-joined per priority, and each manifest independently contributes its BE/FE signals to the scoring matrix. Commands for the subdir are determined by the highest-priority detector, not concatenated.
- **Re-run installer on existing project:** all already-filled fields (non-placeholder, non-blank) are preserved unchanged. Detection runs again but produces no changes to those fields.
- **`/cc-init` on a project with a CLAUDE.md already fully filled:** detect-stack runs, JSON is produced, all fields found to be non-placeholder → zero questions asked, zero writes performed.

### Error cases

- **CI/CD non-interactive mode:** if the environment variable `CI=true` (or `CI=1`) is set, or if `process.stdin.isTTY` is `false`, the installer and `/cc-init` suppress all interactive questions entirely. Any field not resolved by `detect-stack.mjs` is left as a `<command>` placeholder in CLAUDE.md — no `readline` prompts are opened, no process hangs. A single non-interactive summary line is written to stderr listing unresolved fields (e.g. `"WARN: fields not auto-detected: lint, format — fill manually"`). CI mode is checked before any interactive flow is initiated.
- **Corrupt or unreadable manifest:** `readManifest` wraps each file read in try/catch; logs to stderr; returns `null` for that manifest. Script continues with remaining detectors. If all detectors return nothing, stdout receives `{}` and exit code is 0.
- **Permission or read error on a workspace subdirectory:** if `fs.promises.readdir` throws for a specific `workspaceDirs` entry (e.g. `EACCES`, `EPERM`), that directory is skipped silently after logging a `WARN` line to stderr. The error does not propagate to the outer `main()` call — all other workspace subdirectories and root detectors continue normally. The skipped directory is removed from `workspaceDirs` in the output JSON.
- **Workspace subdirectory with no valid manifest files:** if a resolved `workspaceDirs` entry contains no recognizable manifest file (after `readdir` succeeds), it contributes zero fields to the merged output. It remains listed in `workspaceDirs` (informational) but no detectors are invoked for it. This is not an error and nothing is logged.
- **Node subprocess stdout/stderr isolation (bash):** the installer captures detect-stack.mjs stdout via command substitution: `detected=$(node scripts/detect-stack.mjs "$root" 2>>"$INSTALL_LOG")`. Stderr is redirected to an install log file (default `~/.claude/install.log`), never to stdout. The command substitution variable `$detected` therefore contains only the clean JSON. If `$INSTALL_LOG` is unset, stderr is redirected to `/dev/null`. In PowerShell: `$raw = node scripts/detect-stack.mjs $root 2>>$installLog | Out-String` — the `2>>` redirect targets the same log file.
- **Loose placeholder matching:** the placeholder detection regex is intentionally permissive to survive minor user edits. Pattern (applied per line, case-insensitive): `/^(\s*-?\s*\w[\w\s]*)\s*:?\s*(<command>|<\s*command\s*>)?\s*(\r?\n|$)/i` — this matches lines where the value after `:` is `<command>` with any internal whitespace, or is blank, regardless of letter casing. After a match, the replacement writes the canonical form `- Key: value` normalized to the template's original casing (key names are never changed, only values are substituted).
- **Mixed custom text and `<command>` placeholder:** a line whose value contains both custom user text and the literal `<command>` token (e.g. `Build: prefix-step && <command>`) is treated as **customized** — the line is not modified. The rule is: if the trimmed value is exactly `<command>` (possibly with internal whitespace, case-insensitive) OR is entirely blank, it is a placeholder. Any other content, even if it contains `<command>` as a substring, is considered a user customization and is preserved unchanged.
- **CLAUDE.md missing or structural headers absent:** if the target CLAUDE.md does not exist at all, the fill step creates the file using `project-template/CLAUDE.md` as the source before applying field values — equivalent to a first-time install. If CLAUDE.md exists but the `## Development Commands` section heading is absent (regex from boundary token rule finds no match), the fill step is skipped entirely with a WARN to stderr: `"WARN: ## Development Commands section not found — skipping auto-fill"`. No content is written or appended; the developer is expected to add the section manually or re-run `install.sh --project` to regenerate from template.
- **Empty or structurally invalid manifest:** after `JSON.parse` succeeds, `readManifest` applies a two-stage validation: (1) type check — `typeof result === 'object' && result !== null && !Array.isArray(result)` must be true; (2) non-empty check — `Object.keys(result).length > 0` must be true (an empty object `{}` has zero keys and is treated the same as a parse failure). If either check fails, `readManifest` logs a warning to stderr and returns `null`. A field value of `null` or `""` within an otherwise-valid manifest is handled at the field level (see Output Contract), not here.
- **Node.js absent or version too low:** before calling `node scripts/detect-stack.mjs`, both `install.sh` and `install.ps1` validate the Node.js runtime: (bash) `node --version 2>/dev/null` captures the version string; the installer extracts the major number via `sed 's/^v\([0-9]*\).*/\1/'` and checks `[ "$major" -ge 18 ]`. (PS) `(node --version 2>$null) -match '^v(\d+)' | Out-Null; [int]$Matches[1] -ge 18`. If `node` is absent or version < 18, a WARN is written to stderr and the detect-stack call is skipped; CLAUDE.md keeps all placeholders; interactive fallback proceeds (or CI mode leaves placeholders silently).
- **Exit code policy:** `detect-stack.mjs` exits 0 in all cases — including corrupt or missing manifests. The script is designed as a best-effort detector; partial results are always preferable to a non-zero exit that would abort an otherwise-functional installer. The only exception: if `fs.promises.readdir` on the **project root itself** throws (not a workspace subdir), the script writes `{}` to stdout, logs the error to stderr, and exits 0. Installer-level fatal errors (missing `project-template/`, unresolvable root path) exit 1 from the installer, never from `detect-stack.mjs`.
- **Atomic write for `_fill_claude_md` (partial write protection):** `_fill_claude_md` writes CLAUDE.md via a two-step atomic pattern: (1) write the modified content to a temp file in the same directory (`CLAUDE.md.tmp.$$`); (2) `mv -f CLAUDE.md.tmp.$$ CLAUDE.md` (bash) or `[System.IO.File]::Replace` (PS). If the process is killed between steps 1 and 2, the original CLAUDE.md is intact. If killed during step 1, the temp file is orphaned and cleaned up on next run (the installer checks for and deletes `CLAUDE.md.tmp.*` before writing). On Windows, `[System.IO.File]::Replace(src, dest, backup)` is used with a `.bak` suffix; the `.bak` file is deleted after successful replace.
- **UTF-8 BOM and other BOM variants:** all file reads use `fs.promises.readFile(path, 'utf8')`. Node.js decodes the bytes as UTF-8 regardless of the BOM marker; a UTF-8 BOM (`0xEF 0xBB 0xBF`, which appears as `﻿` in the decoded string) is stripped via `.replace(/^﻿/, '')` immediately after reading. UTF-16 and UTF-32 BOMs are not decoded correctly by `'utf8'` mode — Node.js returns garbled bytes. These are treated as corrupt files: `JSON.parse` will throw (caught by `readManifest`'s try/catch), and the manifest is skipped with a WARN. No attempt is made to detect and re-decode UTF-16/UTF-32 files; developers must save manifests as UTF-8 without BOM or with UTF-8 BOM only.
- **Internal symlinks to valid subdirectories within root:** symlinks whose `realpath` resolves to a path inside the project root boundary (passes the `startsWith(rootRealpath + path.sep)` check) are treated identically to real directories — they are walked, their contents are `readdir`-ed, and their `readdir` results are passed to detectors. The `realpath`-based visited Set prevents the same physical directory from being scanned twice even if multiple symlinks point to it.
- **Hidden directories and system dotfiles in root sweep:** the root `readdir` result includes entries starting with `.` (e.g. `.git`, `.github`, `.vscode`, `node_modules`). The workspace expansion algorithm and all detectors explicitly skip any entry whose name starts with `.` or equals `node_modules`. This exclusion is applied at the `readdir` filter step, before any `isDirectory()` check. The root-level file list passed to detectors still includes dotfiles (e.g. `.eslintrc`, `.nvmrc`) since these are valid manifest signals — the exclusion applies only to directory traversal, not to file-level detection.
- **readdir I/O timeout:** each `fs.promises.readdir` call is wrapped with a `Promise.race` against a 10-second timeout (`setTimeout` with a reject). If any single `readdir` call does not resolve within 10 seconds, that directory is skipped with `WARN: readdir timeout — skipped: <path>`. The timeout is per-directory, not per-script — the overall script may still take longer if many directories each take close to 10 seconds. The timeout value is hard-coded; no environment variable override is provided.
- **Zero-byte manifest files:** before calling `readFile`, the script checks `(await fs.promises.stat(path)).size`. If size is 0, the file is skipped with `WARN: zero-byte manifest skipped: <path>` and `readManifest` returns `null`. This is distinct from the 512 KB cap — zero-byte files skip the read entirely.
- **Fatal stderr error schema:** if a fatal error occurs in `main()` before any JSON is written to stdout (e.g. `readdir` on the project root throws), the script writes a JSON error object to **stderr** in the form `{"error":"<message>","code":"<POSIX error code or UNKNOWN>"}` and exits 0. Stdout receives `{}\n` as always. Callers that capture stderr separately can parse this object for diagnostic purposes. Non-fatal warnings (individual file or subdir errors) remain as plain text `WARN:` lines on stderr, not JSON.
- **Globally ignored directories:** the following directory names are always excluded from workspace expansion and from the `workspaceDirs` list, regardless of glob patterns or monorepo indicators: `node_modules`, `.git`, `.svn`, `.hg`, `.expo`, `.dart_tool`, `.pub-cache`, `__pycache__`, `.gradle`, `.m2`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `.cache`, `.parcel-cache`. These are checked against the `name` property of each `readdir` entry (case-sensitive on POSIX, case-insensitive on Windows) before `isDirectory()` is tested. Hidden directories not in this list (starting with `.`) are still excluded from traversal by the general hidden-dir rule.
- **False positives from commented-out `packages:` in YAML:** the top-level key scanner for `melos.yaml` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` detects the `packages:` section start using the pattern `/^packages\s*:/` applied only to lines where the **first non-whitespace character is not `#`**. A line like `# packages:` (commented out) is skipped before the pattern is tested. Indented `packages:` (e.g. `  packages:`) is also ignored — the section header must be at column 0 (zero leading spaces).
- **Execution timeout and file-size limits:** `detect-stack.mjs` enforces two resource guards: (1) **per-file read size cap** — any manifest file larger than 512 KB is skipped with `WARN: manifest too large (>512KB), skipped: <path>`; the cap is applied before `readFile` by checking `fs.statSync(path).size`; (2) **workspace subdir count cap** — if the total number of resolved `workspaceDirs` entries (after dedup) exceeds 200, a WARN is emitted and the list is truncated to the first 200 entries in sorted order. These limits prevent resource exhaustion in enterprise monorepos with hundreds of packages. Both caps are hard-coded constants in the script; no environment variable override is provided (intentional — raising them requires a code change and review).
- **Runtime exceptions during sub-workspace file reads:** each manifest read within a workspace subdir is wrapped in its own isolated try/catch block inside `readManifest`. An exception thrown while reading a file in workspace subdir `X` does not propagate to the read loop for workspace subdir `Y` or to the root detector. The outer `workspaceDirs` iteration loop is also wrapped in a try/catch at the per-directory level, ensuring any unexpected error in one subdir's entire processing block is caught, logged to stderr, and execution continues with the next subdir.
- **PS 5.1 `ConvertFrom-Json` failure:** isolated try/catch sets `$detected = $null`; installer proceeds with full interactive fallback.
- **CLAUDE.md missing or read-only:** installer logs a warning to stderr and skips the fill step; no crash.
- **Absolute path resolution fails:** fallback to `$PWD` / `$(pwd)`. Log warning to stderr.
- **`project-template/` directory missing or inaccessible:** installer prints a fatal error to stderr (`"ERROR: project-template/ not found at <path>. Re-run install.sh from the code-conductor repo root."`) and exits with code 1 immediately — before any file copy or detect-stack call. No partial installation is performed. This check runs before the detect-stack invocation so that a missing template never leaves CLAUDE.md in a half-written state.
- **Special characters in detected values (bash) — complete escape matrix:** `_fill_claude_md` passes each value through a sequential escape function before inserting it into the `sed` replacement string. Escape order (each step applied to the output of the previous): (1) `\` → `\\`; (2) `&` → `\&`; (3) `|` → `\|` (sed delimiter); (4) newlines → single space (BSD/GNU sed portability). Characters that require **no escaping** in sed's replacement string when the command is single-quoted in bash: `'` (single quote), `"` (double quote), `$` (dollar sign). Single quotes cannot appear inside a single-quoted string at all — if a value contains `'`, the sed command must be constructed via `printf '%s'` piping rather than inline shell quoting. The recommended pattern: `printf '%s\n' "$escaped_value" | sed -e "s|<pattern>|$(cat -)|"` avoids all shell-interpolation risks for the replacement value. The `\`-first ordering ensures that the sequences `\1`–`\9` (which sed treats as back-references in replacement strings) are automatically neutralized: any `\N` in the original value becomes `\\N` after the `\`-escape step, which sed interprets as a literal backslash followed by a literal digit, never a back-reference. No separate digit-sequence escaping step is required. Replacement is performed with `sed` using the `|` delimiter (not `/`) to avoid conflicts with path-containing values. **Newline handling:** literal newlines in a detected value are replaced with a space character before the sed call — this avoids the BSD-vs-GNU-sed divergence entirely. **Read flag:** when the installer shell script reads the node output line-by-line it must use `while IFS= read -r line; do` — the `-r` flag prevents bash from consuming backslashes during the read, ensuring backslash sequences in detected values survive intact into the escape function.
- **PowerShell CLAUDE.md write encoding (UTF-8 without BOM):** when `Set-ClaudeMdFields` writes CLAUDE.md, it must use `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(path, content, [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8)` — **not** `Out-File`, `Set-Content`, or `Add-Content`, which default to UTF-16 LE (with BOM) in PowerShell 5.1. `[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` in .NET 4.x emits UTF-8 **without** BOM (unlike `[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($true)` which emits with BOM). This applies to both the atomic temp-file write and any fallback direct write.
- **PowerShell console output encoding for non-ASCII characters:** at the start of `install.ps1`, before any output or node invocation, set `[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` and `$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8`. This ensures that non-ASCII characters in detected manifest values (e.g. project names or descriptions containing accented characters, CJK, or emoji) are transmitted correctly through the `| Out-String` pipeline and through `ConvertTo-Json`. Without this, Windows PowerShell 5.1 defaults to the system code page (often cp1252 or cp932), which silently corrupts characters outside the ASCII range.
- **Concurrent install race condition:** if two installer processes run simultaneously against the same target directory, each may read the same CLAUDE.md before either writes, producing a last-write-wins race on the file. Mitigation: the atomic write pattern (`CLAUDE.md.tmp.$$` + `mv -f` in bash; `[System.IO.File]::Replace` in PS) makes the final write atomic at the filesystem level, preventing torn writes. However, detection-phase races (both processes detect the same unset fields and both attempt to fill them) are not prevented — the second write wins and may overwrite a value written by the first. No advisory lock is implemented; the spec accepts this as an acceptable limitation for a developer-tool installer that is not designed for concurrent execution. Mitigation guidance in WARN output: if `$INSTALL_LOG` already exists and was modified within the last 5 seconds, the installer emits `WARN: another install process may be running — consider waiting`.
- **Target CLAUDE.md locked by another process:** on Windows, if the atomic write to `CLAUDE.md.tmp.$$` or the `[System.IO.File]::Replace` call fails with a file-lock error (`IOException`, `UnauthorizedAccessException`), the installer retries once after a 500 ms sleep. If the retry also fails, it logs the error to stderr and exits with a WARN (not an error) — the original CLAUDE.md is never modified in this case (the temp file is cleaned up).
- **Scripts relying on environment variables:** detected commands (e.g. `DATABASE_URL=$DB npm test`) that reference environment variables are captured verbatim into CLAUDE.md. The script makes no attempt to resolve or validate environment variable references — they are treated as opaque strings. The developer is expected to set the required variables in their shell or CI environment before running the detected command.
- **Special characters in detected values (PowerShell):** `Set-ClaudeMdFields` performs the replacement with `-replace` using a regex-literal LHS and a plain string RHS. The LHS (placeholder pattern) is wrapped in `[regex]::Escape`. The RHS (detected value) is a plain PowerShell string variable — PowerShell's `-replace` operator does **not** interpret `\` in the replacement string as a regex escape; backslashes are passed through verbatim. This means Windows paths such as `C:\Users\foo\project` are preserved without any additional escaping. The only character that requires escaping in the RHS is `$`, which must be doubled to `$$` to prevent PowerShell from interpreting `$1`, `$2`, etc. as back-reference captures.

## Detection Rules

### Java / JVM

- **Spring Boot** (highest-priority Java sub-detector): `pom.xml` present and contains `spring-boot-starter` in any `<artifactId>` element, OR `build.gradle` / `build.gradle.kts` present and the file text contains `spring-boot-starter` as a string. Commands: `./mvnw spring-boot:run` / `./gradlew bootRun` (prefer wrapper scripts if present, else `mvn`/`gradle`). Build: `./mvnw package -DskipTests` / `./gradlew build`. Test: `./mvnw test` / `./gradlew test`. Lint: N/A. Format: N/A.
- **Quarkus**: `pom.xml` or `build.gradle` contains `quarkus-core` or `io.quarkus`. Commands: `./mvnw quarkus:dev` / `./gradlew quarkusDev`.
- **Vanilla Java**: `pom.xml` or `build.gradle` present without recognized framework. Prefer `./mvnw` over `mvn`; prefer `./gradlew` over `gradle`. Maven commands: build = `./mvnw package`, test = `./mvnw test`. Gradle commands: build = `./gradlew build`, test = `./gradlew test`.
- **Scala / SBT**: `build.sbt` present in the root file list. Commands: build = `sbt compile`, test = `sbt test`, lint = `sbt scalafmt --check`, format = `sbt scalafmt`, setup = `sbt update`. Stack tag: `"scala"`.

### .NET / C#

- Detection signature: one or more `*.csproj` files present in the root file list, OR one or more `*.sln` files present. Use `fs.promises.readdir` results (already available) — no glob expansion needed; check each filename against `/\.csproj$|\.sln$/i`. Commands: build = `dotnet build`, test = `dotnet test`, lint = `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, format = `dotnet format`, setup = `dotnet restore`. Stack tag: `"csharp"`. If a `*.sln` file is found, setup becomes `dotnet restore <sln-file>` using the first `.sln` filename found.

### Go

- Detection: `go.mod` present. Version extraction: read `go.mod` (first 20 lines via `fs.promises.readFile`); find the line matching `/^go\s+(\d+\.\d+)/`; extract the version string (e.g. `"1.23"`). Emit as `"goVersion": "1.23"` in the output JSON. Commands: build = `go build ./...`, test = `go test ./...`, lint = `golangci-lint run` (emit only if `golangci-lint` is listed in any tool config; otherwise omit lint), format = `gofmt -w .`, setup = `go mod download`. Stack tag: `"go"`.

### Rust

- Detection: `Cargo.toml` present. Read `Cargo.toml` for `[package] name` and `version` fields using line-by-line scan (no TOML parser — extract first match of `/^name\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/` and `/^version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/` within the `[package]` section, defined as lines between `[package]` and the next `[` header). Commands: build = `cargo build`, test = `cargo test`, lint = `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, format = `cargo fmt`, setup = `cargo fetch`. Stack tag: `"rust"`.

### Native Mobile

- **iOS (Xcode)**: `*.xcodeproj` or `*.xcworkspace` present in the root file list (check each filename against `/\.(xcodeproj|xcworkspace)$/`). If both present, prefer `xcworkspace` (CocoaPods integrated). Commands: build = `xcodebuild -workspace <name>.xcworkspace -scheme <name> -sdk iphonesimulator build` (substitute first-found filenames). Test = `xcodebuild test`. Lint = N/A. Format = `swiftformat .` (only if `Podfile` references `SwiftFormat` or `swiftformat` is in PATH detection — otherwise omit). Setup = `pod install` if `Podfile` present, else `swift package resolve`. Stack tag: `"swift"`.
- **Android (native Gradle)**: `android/build.gradle` or `android/build.gradle.kts` present (checked by probing `<root>/android/` — counts as one additional `readdir` call, attributed to the Android detector, not the monorepo algorithm). Commands: build = `./gradlew assembleDebug`, test = `./gradlew test`, lint = `./gradlew lint`, format = N/A, setup = `./gradlew dependencies`. Stack tag: `"kotlin"` if `*.kt` files found in `android/app/src/`, else `"java"`.

### React Native vs Ionic vs Capacitor

All three share a `package.json` entry point; differentiation is by additional file markers and dependency names:

1. **Ionic**: `ionic.config.json` present in root file list → stack `"ionic"`. Commands: build = `ionic build`, test = `npm test`, setup = `npm install`.
2. **Capacitor standalone** (non-Ionic): `capacitor.config.json` or `capacitor.config.ts` present, AND no `ionic.config.json` → stack `"capacitor"`. Commands: build = `npx cap build`, setup = `npm install && npx cap sync`.
3. **React Native (Expo)**: `react-native` + `expo` in `package.json` dependencies → stack `"react-native-expo"`. Commands: build = `expo build`, test = `jest`, setup = `npm install`.
4. **React Native (bare)**: `react-native` in `package.json` dependencies without `expo`, `ionic.config.json`, or `capacitor.config.*` → stack `"react-native"`. Commands: build = `react-native bundle`, test = `jest`, setup = `npm install`.

Precedence: Ionic > Capacitor > React Native Expo > React Native bare. These checks run before the standard React detector so that a project with both `react-native` and `react` in deps is never misclassified as a plain React web app.

### Flutter

- Detection: `pubspec.yaml` present. Flutter is confirmed by `pubspec.yaml` containing `flutter:` as a top-level YAML key (line-scan: any line matching `/^flutter\s*:/`). Commands: build = `flutter build`, test = `flutter test`, lint = `flutter analyze`, format = `dart format .`, setup = `flutter pub get`. Stack tag: `"flutter"`. These commands override any generic platform commands from Melos or the monorepo detector — Flutter CLI is always the authoritative command source when confirmed.

### Dependencies vs devDependencies for Scoring

- **Production scoring signals** (`dependencies` only): framework detection for `FE_SCORE` and `BE_SCORE` (React, Express, Go runtime deps, etc.) checks `dependencies` exclusively. A framework listed only in `devDependencies` (e.g. React added as a dev dep by mistake, or a backend framework used only in test fixtures) does **not** contribute to the scoring matrix. This prevents devDependency-only test utilities (e.g. `jest`, `vitest`, `ts-jest`) from inflating the BE or FE score.
- **Tool detection** (`devDependencies` only): lint/format/test command detection (e.g. `eslint`, `prettier`, `vitest`, `jest`) reads `devDependencies`. A tool listed only in `dependencies` is still recognized (belt-and-suspenders), but `devDependencies` is the canonical location.
- **Stack tag detection** (both): framework identification for the `stack` string (e.g. detecting `react` → `"typescript"`) checks both `dependencies` and `devDependencies`, since some projects (particularly libraries) ship frameworks as peer or dev deps.

### Infrastructure and Container Signals

Container and infrastructure files are detected independently of the primary stack and contribute a `"infra"` field to the output JSON.

- **Dockerfile / docker-compose:** `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.*`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, or `compose.yml` present in root file list → `"infra": "docker"`.
- **Kubernetes:** `k8s/` or `kubernetes/` directory, or any `*.yaml` in root whose filename contains `deployment`, `service`, or `ingress` → `"infra": "kubernetes"` (overrides `"docker"` if both present).
- **Terraform:** `*.tf` files in root → `"infra": "terraform"`.
- **GitHub Actions:** `.github/workflows/` directory present → `"infra": "github-actions"` (does not override other infra indicators; emitted as a separate `"ci"` field: `"ci": "github-actions"`).
- Detection is additive: `infra` captures the highest-priority infrastructure signal; `ci` captures CI/CD platform independently.

### Conflicting Dependency Versions Across Monorepo Packages

When multiple workspace subdirs declare the same dependency at different versions (e.g. `apps/web` has `"react": "18"` and `apps/admin` has `"react": "19"`), version conflicts are **not** reported and do not affect detection — the detector only checks for dependency presence, not version values. The highest-priority subdir (first in sorted `workspaceDirs` order) determines which version-pinned value (e.g. Angular major) is extracted. Version conflicts are a package-manager concern outside the scope of this script.

### Architectural Pattern Detection

detect-stack.mjs emits an `"architecture"` field when directory structure signals a known architectural pattern. Detection is heuristic and best-effort. The same directory name signals apply to all stacks (JS, Go, Dart, Rust, Java, etc.) — architecture detection is language-agnostic. For Go repositories: `internal/` and `cmd/` are standard Go project layout conventions and are already captured by the BE scoring matrix; `domain/` and `ports/` inside a Go repo signal Clean Architecture identically to a TypeScript repo.

- **Clean Architecture / Hexagonal:** presence of directories named `domain/`, `application/`, `infrastructure/`, `ports/`, or `adapters/` in root or in a primary `src/` subdirectory → `"architecture": "clean"`.
- **MVC:** presence of directories named `controllers/`, `models/`, `views/` (or `views` inside `src/`) → `"architecture": "mvc"`.
- **Layered (generic):** presence of `service/` + `repository/` (or `dao/`) → `"architecture": "layered"`.
- If no pattern matches, `architecture` is omitted. Patterns are checked in order: clean > mvc > layered. Only one value is emitted.

### Project Name Resolution

When writing the `name` field to CLAUDE.md: the value from the manifest (e.g. `package.json` `"name"`, `go.mod` `module` directive last path segment, `Cargo.toml` `[package] name`) takes priority over the root directory name. **Fallback chain (applied in order, first non-empty result wins):** (1) highest-priority manifest name across all detected manifests; (2) `path.basename(rootRealpath)` — the literal root folder name (real path, not symlink alias). If every detected manifest is missing a `name` field or has an empty/null value, the folder name is always used as the final fallback. The `name` field is therefore never omitted from the output JSON when a project root can be resolved. The `go.mod` module path (e.g. `github.com/org/myrepo`) is trimmed to its last path segment (`myrepo`) before use as the name value.

### Internal Quote Escaping in `install.sh`

When `_fill_claude_md` receives a detected value that contains literal `"` characters (e.g. a `description` field like `A "fast" web server`), the value must be escaped before being interpolated into the sed command string. The escape sequence: replace `"` with `\"` (backslash-double-quote) — applied **after** the `\`-first general escaping step so the added `\` is not re-escaped. The sed command is always wrapped in single quotes (`'…'`) in bash, so `"` has no shell significance inside it; the escape is strictly for sed's replacement string parser, which does not treat `"` specially — therefore `"` in values requires **no escaping** in sed at all. The installer must **not** double-escape quotes: passing the value through shell interpolation before the `sed` call is the actual risk; `_fill_claude_md` must not use `eval` or unquoted variable expansion. Use `printf '%s' "$value" | sed …` to feed the value safely.

### Database Signatures

Database presence is detected independently of the primary stack and emits a `"db"` field in the output JSON.

- **Prisma**: `prisma/schema.prisma` or `schema.prisma` present in root → `"db": "prisma"`.
- **Migration directories**: directory named `migrations/` or `db/migrate/` present in root `readdir` results (`isDirectory()` true) → `"db": "migrations"` (if not already set by a higher-priority indicator).
- **Database driver packages** (from `package.json` `dependencies`/`devDependencies`): `pg` or `@prisma/client` → `"db": "postgres"`; `mysql2` or `mysql` → `"db": "mysql"`; `mongodb` or `mongoose` → `"db": "mongodb"`; `sqlite3` or `better-sqlite3` → `"db": "sqlite"`. Priority: Prisma > migration dir > driver package.
- For non-JS stacks: `go.mod` containing `database/sql`, `gorm.io/gorm`, or `entgo.io/ent` → `"db": "go-orm"`. `Cargo.toml` containing `diesel` or `sqlx` → `"db": "rust-db"`. `pom.xml`/`build.gradle` containing `spring-data` or `hibernate` → `"db": "jpa"`.

## Project Classification

detect-stack.mjs computes `projectType` and `layeredArchitecture` using a scoring matrix applied after all detectors have run.

### Scoring matrix

Each detected signal contributes points to `FE_SCORE` and `BE_SCORE`:

| Signal | FE | BE |
|---|---|---|
| `react`, `vue`, `angular`, `next`, `svelte`, `ionic`, `capacitor` dep | +3 | 0 |
| `src/` or `public/` or `static/` or `assets/` dir in root | +1 | 0 |
| `express`, `nestjs`, `fastify`, `hono`, `koa` dep | 0 | +3 |
| `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `*.csproj` present | 0 | +3 |
| `api/` or `server/` or `cmd/` or `internal/` dir in root | 0 | +2 |
| `db` field set (any value) | 0 | +1 |
| `react-native`, `expo`, `flutter`, `swift`, `kotlin` stack | 0 (mobile) | 0 (mobile) |

**Classification rules** (applied in priority order — first matching rule wins):

1. **Infrastructure/Automation**: `infra` field is set (any value: `"docker"`, `"kubernetes"`, or `"terraform"`), AND **both** `FE_SCORE < 2` AND `BE_SCORE < 2` → `projectType = "infra"`, `layeredArchitecture = "N/A"`. A repo containing only Dockerfiles and CI pipelines with no application manifests (`package.json`, `go.mod`, etc.) produces `FE_SCORE = 0`, `BE_SCORE = 0` and an `infra` signal, landing here. If the same repo also contains `go.mod` for a build tool (`BE_SCORE = 3`), rule 1 does not fire — it falls through to rule 6 (BACKEND_ONLY), because the application code takes precedence over the infra signal.
2. **Mobile**: stack is `react-native`, `react-native-expo`, `flutter`, `swift`, or `kotlin` → `projectType = "mobile"`, `layeredArchitecture = "N/A"`. Mobile wins over all scoring-based rules.
3. **FULLSTACK**: `FE_SCORE >= 2` AND `BE_SCORE >= 2` → `projectType = "fullstack"`, `layeredArchitecture = "fullstack"`.
4. **Balanced tie-breaker** (`FE_SCORE == BE_SCORE` and both `>= 2`): classify as `"fullstack"`. A perfectly balanced score is the strongest signal of a fullstack project; there is no asymmetric tie-breaking. The `layeredArchitecture` field is `"fullstack"` in this case.
5. **FRONTEND_ONLY**: `FE_SCORE >= 2` AND `BE_SCORE < 2` → `projectType = "frontend"`, `layeredArchitecture = "fe-only"`.
6. **BACKEND_ONLY**: `BE_SCORE >= 2` AND `FE_SCORE < 2` → `projectType = "backend"`, `layeredArchitecture = "be-only"`.
7. **UNKNOWN**: neither score reaches 2 → `projectType = "library"`, `layeredArchitecture = "unknown"`. Libraries, SDKs, CLI tools, and blank repos all fall here.

**`projectType` is always a single exclusive string.** No compound values (`"fullstack-mobile"`, `"frontend+infra"`) are ever emitted. Rules are applied in the listed order; the first match determines the output.

### Same-layer precedence for multi-manifest environments

When multiple language manifests coexist at the same directory layer (e.g. `package.json` + `go.mod` + `Cargo.toml` all at the root), the classification is determined by the **combined score** across all manifests at that layer, not by the primary stack detector alone. Each manifest independently contributes its BE/FE signals to the matrix; `stack` is still the `/`-joined concatenation of all detected languages in priority order. This prevents a polyglot workspace from being misclassified as single-stack: a repo with `package.json` (React) + `go.mod` will score `FE=3, BE=3` and be classified `FULLSTACK`, not `FRONTEND_ONLY`.

## Output Contract

`detect-stack.mjs` writes exactly one JSON object to stdout. All properties are optional; omitted properties signal "not detected" and trigger interactive fallback. Every present string value has been `.trim()`-ed before output.

```jsonc
{
  "name":        "string | undefined",  // project name (from manifest name field)
  "description": "string | undefined",  // project description
  "stack":       "string | undefined",  // e.g. "typescript", "go", "typescript/go"
  "build":       "string | undefined",  // build command (e.g. "npm run build")
  "test":        "string | undefined",  // test command
  "lint":        "string | undefined",  // lint command
  "format":      "string | undefined",  // format command
  "setup":       "string | undefined",  // setup command (e.g. "npm install")
  "packageManager": "npm | yarn | pnpm | bun | undefined",
  "monorepo":    "boolean | undefined", // true when workspace indicator detected
  "workspaceDirs": "string[] | undefined", // resolved absolute subdirectory paths scanned
  "goVersion":   "string | undefined",  // e.g. "1.23"; only when Go detected
  "db":          "string | undefined",  // e.g. "prisma", "postgres", "mysql", "mongodb", "sqlite", "go-orm", "rust-db", "jpa", "migrations"
  "projectType": "frontend | backend | fullstack | mobile | library | infra | undefined",
  "layeredArchitecture": "fe-only | be-only | fullstack | N/A | unknown | undefined",
  "architecture": "clean | mvc | layered | undefined",
  "infra":        "docker | kubernetes | terraform | undefined",
  "ci":           "github-actions | undefined"
}
```

- All values are plain strings (no nested objects). Installers write values verbatim — no secondary unescaping.
- **Null and empty-string fields:** if a manifest field value is `null`, `undefined`, or resolves to an empty string after `.trim()`, the corresponding output property is **omitted entirely** from the JSON object (not emitted as `null` or `""`). An omitted property signals "not detected" to callers and triggers interactive fallback — it is never written to CLAUDE.md.
- **`db` field — always a single string, cross-layer in monorepos:** the `db` field emits the highest-priority database indicator found across all layers (root + all workspace subdirs). The priority chain (Prisma > migration dir > driver package > go-orm/rust-db/jpa) is applied globally; a Prisma indicator in any workspace subdir beats a `migrations/` dir at the root. Multiple technologies produce only one `db` value; a future `dbs` array field (separate spec) will enumerate all detected databases per layer.
- **`projectType` — single exclusive tag only:** `projectType` is always one of six enumerated string values: `frontend`, `backend`, `fullstack`, `mobile`, `library`, `infra`. Compound tags (`"fullstack-mobile"`, `"frontend+infra"`) are never emitted. Rules are applied in strict priority order (see Project Classification); the first matching rule wins.
- **stdout-only guarantee for `detect-stack.mjs`:** the script never writes to `process.stdout` except for the single final `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n'` call in `main()`. All intermediate output (warnings, debug, version info) goes to `process.stderr` exclusively. Any `console.log` call in the script is a spec violation.
- **Empty-repository output format:** when zero detectors produce any result (no recognized manifest files anywhere), the script emits exactly `{}\n` to stdout — a valid empty JSON object, UTF-8, no BOM, no trailing properties. This is the same as the corrupt-manifest fallback. Callers must handle `{}` as a fully valid (all-fields-absent) response.
- **CLAUDE.md Development Commands block boundary:** the placeholder-fill algorithm locates the `## Development Commands` section by scanning for a line matching `/^##\s+Development\s+Commands\s*(\r?\n|$)/i` (case-insensitive, optional trailing whitespace). Field lines within the section are recognized until the next `##`-level heading or end-of-file. The installer never writes outside this section boundary; if the section is absent, the fill step is skipped with a WARN.
- **`architecture`, `infra`, `ci` fields:** these optional string fields follow the same null-omission rule — omitted when not detected; never emitted as `null` or `""`.
- **Stdout/stderr isolation restatement:** `detect-stack.mjs` writes exactly one JSON object to stdout (no debug lines, no progress indicators, no blank lines before or after). All other output uses `process.stderr.write`. This contract holds regardless of `CC_GUARD_DEBUG` or other environment variables.
- **Lexicographic sort — case-sensitive:** `workspaceDirs` is sorted using `Array.prototype.sort()` with no arguments or comparator, which in V8 (Node.js) performs Unicode code-point order: uppercase letters (`A`–`Z`, U+0041–U+005A) sort before lowercase (`a`–`z`, U+0061–U+007A). This is deterministic across all Node.js 18+ runtimes but may differ from OS-level directory listing on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS, Windows). The spec explicitly chooses case-sensitive Unicode order as the canonical sort regardless of host OS filesystem sensitivity.
- **Description field update on re-run:** the `description` field (and all other fields) follow the same non-overwrite rule — if the CLAUDE.md line already contains a non-placeholder, non-blank value, it is never overwritten, even if the manifest's description has changed since the last install run. The only way to re-detect and re-fill an already-filled field is to manually reset it to `<command>` or blank, then re-run the installer. This is intentional: developer customizations must never be silently replaced by automated detection.
- **Cleanup of dangling auto-generated comments:** on re-run, the installer does not scan for or remove auto-generated comments from previous runs. No auto-generated comments are written during any run (the fill step only replaces field values, not surrounding lines). If a developer manually added `# auto-detected` comments adjacent to fields, those lines are preserved unchanged. There is no cleanup phase.
- `workspaceDirs` is informational; installers do not iterate it — all merging is done inside the script.
- Additional properties may be added in future versions; installers must ignore unknown keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node scripts/detect-stack.mjs <dir>` prints only valid JSON to stdout; all warnings/errors go to stderr; exit code is always 0
- [ ] Output format is exactly `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n'`, UTF-8, no BOM
- [ ] `main()` calls `fs.promises.readdir` for the project root exactly once; when a monorepo indicator is present, one additional `readdir` is issued per workspace subdirectory (listed under `workspaces` or inferred); no detector calls `readdir` independently
- [ ] Detector execution order (first match wins per field): Ionic → Capacitor → React Native (Expo) → React Native (bare) → Flutter/Melos → Angular (version-pinned) → Next.js → NestJS → React → Vue → bare TypeScript/Node → Go → Python → Rust → Scala/SBT → Spring Boot → Quarkus → Java (Maven → Gradle) → .NET (csproj/sln) → iOS (Xcode) → Android (native) → generic fallback
- [ ] Spring Boot sub-detector: `pom.xml` content contains `spring-boot-starter` in any `<artifactId>` OR `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` text contains `spring-boot-starter`; stack tag `"spring-boot"`; preferred wrapper scripts (`./mvnw`, `./gradlew`) used when present
- [ ] .NET detection: any `*.csproj` or `*.sln` in root file list; stack tag `"csharp"`; setup command includes `.sln` filename when a solution file is present
- [ ] Go version: `go.mod` line-scanned for `/^go\s+(\d+\.\d+)/`; result emitted as `"goVersion"` string in output JSON
- [ ] Scala/SBT: `build.sbt` in root → stack `"scala"`, commands `sbt compile/test/scalafmt`
- [ ] Rust: `Cargo.toml` in root → stack `"rust"`, commands `cargo build/test/clippy/fmt/fetch`; `[package] name` and `version` extracted via line-scan without TOML parser
- [ ] iOS: `*.xcodeproj` or `*.xcworkspace` in root → stack `"swift"`; prefer workspace over project; `pod install` if `Podfile` present
- [ ] Android: `android/build.gradle` or `android/build.gradle.kts` present → stack `"kotlin"` or `"java"` based on `*.kt` file presence; one additional `readdir` issued for `<root>/android/`
- [ ] Ionic/Capacitor/React Native precedence: Ionic > Capacitor > RN Expo > RN bare > plain React — none classified as plain React web app if mobile markers present
- [ ] `"db"` field: Prisma > migration dir > driver package > go-orm/rust-db/jpa; never overwrites a higher-priority db indicator
- [ ] `projectType` and `layeredArchitecture` computed from scoring matrix; mobile stacks always produce `"mobile"` / `"N/A"` regardless of score; `library` is the fallback when neither FE_SCORE nor BE_SCORE reaches 2
- [ ] Same-layer polyglot classification: all manifests at the same layer contribute to the scoring matrix independently; a React + Go repo scores FE=3, BE=3 → `fullstack`
- [ ] Python sub-detector disambiguation (checked in order, first match wins): `uv.lock` present → uv (`uv sync`); `pyproject.toml` containing `[tool.uv]` section → uv (`uv sync`); `pyproject.toml` containing `[tool.poetry]` section → poetry (`poetry install`); `poetry.lock` present → poetry (`poetry install`); `Pipfile` present → pipenv (`pipenv install`); `pyproject.toml` containing `[tool.hatch]` section → hatch (`hatch env create`); `hatch.toml` present → hatch (`hatch env create`); `requirements.txt` present → pip (`pip install -r requirements.txt`); `pyproject.toml` present without recognized tool section → pip fallback (`pip install -e .`)
- [ ] Monorepo detection: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` present, or `pkg.workspaces` array, or `melos.yaml` → commands adjusted (e.g. `pnpm -r build`, `melos bootstrap`)
- [ ] All string values from manifests are `.trim()`-ed before being placed in the output JSON
- [ ] Parsed JSON property values are written to CLAUDE.md as-is (no secondary regex unescaping); `ConvertFrom-Json` / `JSON.parse` guarantees unescaped runtime strings
- [ ] Placeholder matching uses CRLF-resilient, non-greedy, line-by-line patterns targeting `<command>` literal or blank after `:\s*`, with an explicit `\s*(\r?\n|$)` suffix to consume optional trailing whitespace before the line ending — never raw key names; a line ending in `<command>   ` (trailing spaces) must match identically to `<command>`
- [ ] Fields in CLAUDE.md that already hold a non-placeholder value are never overwritten by installer or `/cc-init`
- [ ] `install.sh --project`: resolves absolute root before calling detect-stack.mjs; fills CLAUDE.md idempotently; re-running the installer on the same project produces byte-identical CLAUDE.md
- [ ] `install.ps1 -Project`: captures stdout via `| Out-String`; `ConvertFrom-Json` in isolated try/catch; no secondary unescape pass
- [ ] `/cc-init` Step 2: asks interactive questions only for fields absent from detected JSON; all resolvable fields written in one `Edit` call
- [ ] `tests/scripts/detect-stack.test.js`: fs/promises fully mocked via Vitest `vi.mock`; covers happy path (package.json with known deps), monorepo (pnpm-workspace.yaml), Angular version pin (root-level and nested workspace), Flutter/melos (melos.yaml with custom `packages:` list), corrupt manifest fail-open, missing manifest returns `{}`, empty `{}` package.json returns `null` from readManifest, non-object JSON (array root) returns `null`, `.trim()` on whitespace-padded values, Go detection, polyglot root (package.json + go.mod → stack = "typescript/go"), workspace subdir scan (Angular dep only in apps/web/package.json), multi-wildcard pattern `packages/*/lib` resolves correctly, workspaceDirs sorted before detector pass (two React subdirs → lexicographically first wins), Python uv/poetry/pip discrimination by lockfile and pyproject.toml section, newline-in-description normalized to space before output
- [ ] `tests/scripts/installer-fill.test.sh` (bash): tests `_fill_claude_md` in isolation — covers: value containing `/`, `&`, `\`, and `$` characters is inserted without breaking sed; placeholder line is replaced; non-placeholder line is preserved unchanged; CRLF line endings in CLAUDE.md are handled correctly
- [ ] `tests/scripts/installer-fill.test.ps1` (PowerShell): tests `Set-ClaudeMdFields` in isolation — covers: value containing `$`, `\`, and regex metacharacters does not cause `-replace` expansion errors; placeholder line is replaced; non-placeholder line is preserved unchanged

## Out of Scope

- Modifying `project.md`, `personal.md`, or any memory file — only CLAUDE.md is touched
- Lock-file dep-tree traversal (lockfile used only to infer package manager: `bun.lockb` → bun, `pnpm-lock.yaml` → pnpm, `yarn.lock` → yarn, else npm; bun takes priority over pnpm/yarn/npm when present)
- Detecting more than one primary framework per project (priority list resolves ambiguity)
- FEAT-016 interactive wizard for blank-workspace / no-manifest case (separate spec)
- Global-only installs (no `--project` flag) — detect-stack is never called
- Generating or modifying `## Architecture Notes`, `## Conventions`, or `## Out of Scope` sections of CLAUDE.md

## System Impact

- `scripts/detect-stack.mjs` — new file; pure ESM; no runtime deps beyond Node built-ins
- `tests/scripts/detect-stack.test.js` — new test file; adds to the Vitest suite
- `tests/scripts/installer-fill.test.sh` — new bash test harness for `_fill_claude_md`; run with `bash tests/scripts/installer-fill.test.sh`
- `tests/scripts/installer-fill.test.ps1` — new PS test harness for `Set-ClaudeMdFields`; run with `pwsh -File tests/scripts/installer-fill.test.ps1` (or `powershell.exe` on Windows 5.1)
- `project-template/.claude/commands/cc-init.md` — Step 2 rewritten to call detect-stack and apply smart merge
- `install.sh` — `--project` path extended with detect-stack call and `_fill_claude_md` helper
- `install.ps1` — `-Project` path extended with detect-stack call and `Set-ClaudeMdFields` helper
- `project-template/CLAUDE.md` — template unchanged (placeholders remain as fallback targets)
- `AGENT-READABLE BACKLOG.md` — BUG-015 checkbox marked `[X]` after verified implementation
- `VERSION` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `README.md` — updated to reflect 1.16.0 release

### Files Requiring Full Read (deferred to /cc-plan)

- `install.sh` — exceeds 30-line cap; `/cc-plan` will read the `--project` branch to identify exact insertion points for `_fill_claude_md` and detect-stack call
- `install.ps1` — same; `/cc-plan` will identify the `-Project` branch insertion points
- `project-template/.claude/commands/cc-init.md` — full read needed to locate Step 2 boundary and identify exact lines to replace

## Complexity Estimate

**XL** — one new Node.js file with 20+ detector branches (including infra/container/architecture signals), project classification matrix with 7 classification rules, DB/infra/CI signal detection, 10 output fields, symlink safety checks, UTF-8 BOM stripping, go.work support, `CC_GLOB_DEPTH` configurable glob expansion with hard ceiling, one new Vitest suite (>30 cases), three new test harnesses (bash + PS + detect-stack), two install script extensions with atomic write and Node version validation, one command file rewrite. No new runtime dependencies. No schema migrations. Complexity upgraded from L due to security hardening, cross-platform edge cases, and expanded output schema.
